prompt: On the study-group page of "A page at a time", where does the counter's template come from?

choices.text: From a `.vue` file that Vite compiled on the way
choices.why: There is no Vite and no `.vue` file there: the folder holds one HTML page and one copy of Vue.

choices.text: From the Python server, which fills the braces before sending
choices.why: `http.server` sends files as they are; it knows nothing of `{{ minutes }}`.

choices.text: From the contents of `#counter`, compiled by Vue in the browser
choices.why: Right. The browser parses the markup as HTML, and the build of Vue that carries the compiler compiles it where it stands.

choices.text: From a string returned by `setup()`
choices.why: `setup()` returns the state the template reads, `{ minutes }`, and no markup at all.

prompt: Every `look` of the planner prints `[vite] connecting...` and `[vite] connected.` before the text. What are those two lines?

choices.text: Errors from the dev server that the page has hidden
choices.why: They are ordinary console messages, not errors; an error would be marked `[error]`.

choices.text: Vite's script in the page, opening a channel to the dev server for your edits
choices.why: Right. That channel is how a saved file reaches the open page without a reload.

choices.text: Playwright starting Chromium
choices.why: Playwright prints nothing into the page's console; these lines come from a script inside the page.

choices.text: Vue announcing that `createApp` has mounted
choices.why: Vue says nothing when it mounts; the lines carry the `[vite]` prefix for a reason.

prompt: The footer's elements carry `data-v-6704560a` on every run, and `App.vue`'s carry a different one. Why are the characters stable?

choices.text: They come from the file's path
choices.why: Right: the same path gives the same characters on every run, and a different file gives different ones.

choices.text: Vue draws them at random once and stores them in the lockfile
choices.why: The lockfile records package versions, nothing about components.

choices.text: They are a count of the components mounted so far
choices.why: A count would change with the order of mounting; these never change for one file.

choices.text: They are the hash of the style block's contents, so only a CSS edit changes them
choices.why: The lesson ties them to the path, not to the rules; editing a rule leaves the attribute alone.

choices.text: A package called `@` in `node_modules`

choices.text: The `planner.js` in the same folder as the importing file

choices.text: `src/planner.js`, whatever the depth of the importing file

choices.text: A file at the root of the project, beside `package.json`

prompt: A component calls `reactive(raw)` twice on the same object `raw`. What do the two calls return?

choices.text: The same proxy both times, and never the object `raw` itself
choices.why: Right. Vue keeps one proxy per original, and never hands back the original itself.

choices.text: Two proxies, which disagree after the first change
choices.why: Vue keeps one proxy per original, so there is no second proxy to disagree.

choices.text: A proxy the first time, and `raw` itself the second
choices.why: `reactive` never returns the original: `session === raw` was `false`.

choices.text: A warning, because an object may only be made reactive once
choices.why: There is no such warning; the only warning in the demo was for `reactive(25)`.

prompt: `week` is `reactive({ planned: 195, done: 75, note: 'verbs' })`, and the data arrives as `loaded = { planned: 220, done: 90 }`. After `Object.assign(week, loaded)`, what does `week` hold?

choices.text: 220, 90, and the old `note`
choices.why: Right. It writes into the same proxy, and leaves alone a property `loaded` lacks: the quieter surprise.

choices.text: `{ planned: 220, done: 90 }`, an exact copy of `loaded`
choices.why: `Object.assign` writes what `loaded` has and removes nothing, so `note` stays.

choices.text: The old values: assigning into a proxy is not seen by the template
choices.why: Writing property by property through the proxy is exactly what the template notices.

choices.text: A second proxy that the template does not hold
choices.why: That is `week = reactive(loaded)`; `Object.assign` keeps the first proxy.

prompt: Anything in the project's ___ folder is served as it is, at the root of the address, which is why the planner can fetch `/courses.json`.

prompt: The planner's `perCourse` returns a new array of new objects each time it runs. A change makes it run again, and every number inside comes out the same. What happens to the template that reads it?

choices.text: Nothing, because Vue compares the objects field by field and finds no change
choices.why: That deep comparison is exactly what Vue does not do for a new object.

choices.text: It throws, because a computed must return the same object each time
choices.why: Returning a new object is allowed; it only costs a redraw.

choices.text: It shows the old numbers until the next change
choices.why: The template reads the new result; the question is only whether it redraws.

choices.text: It redraws anyway
choices.why: Right. Vue 3.4 skips the redraw for an unchanged number or string, and does not look inside a new object to compare.

prompt: `label = computed(() => (showHours.value ? `${hours.value} hours` : `${minutes.value} minutes`))`. While `showHours` is false, `hours` changes. What does `label` do?

choices.text: It recomputes, because `hours` is written in its function
choices.why: Being written in the function is not enough; it has to have been read on the last run.

choices.text: Nothing at all, because its last run never read `hours`
choices.why: Right. The dependencies are whatever the last run read: `showHours` and `minutes`.

choices.text: It is stale until `showHours` changes, and then shows the wrong hours
choices.why: When `showHours` turns true the function runs again and reads the current `hours`.

choices.text: Vue warns that a computed read a value conditionally
choices.why: A condition inside a computed is ordinary; nothing warns.

prompt: In `WritableHours`, the setter stores `Math.round(value * 60)`. After `hours.value = 0.01`, how many minutes does `minutes` hold?
Which of these array methods change the array they are called on, and so have no business inside a computed? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: `reverse`
choices.why: Right: it reverses in place and returns the same array.

choices.text: `toSorted`
choices.why: It returns a sorted copy and leaves the original alone, which is why the planner uses it.

choices.text: `splice`
choices.why: Right: it removes and inserts in place.

choices.text: `filter`
choices.why: It builds a new array; the planner's `sessionsInWeek` is one.

choices.text: `sort`
choices.why: Right: `byDateWrong` sorted `sessions.value` itself this way.

prompt: Since Vue 3.5, `deep` also takes a number. What does `{ deep: 1 }` watch on a ref holding the list of sessions?

choices.text: Only the first session in the list
choices.why: The number is a depth, not an index.

choices.text: The array and its items, but not inside the items
choices.why: Right: a push is seen, a change to one session's minutes is not.

choices.text: Everything, as `deep: true` does, but at most once
choices.why: That is `once: true`; the number limits depth, not the number of runs.

choices.text: Nothing new: any number is read as `true`

prompt: What is `watchPostEffect`?

choices.text: A watcher that runs after the component is removed
choices.why: Removal stops watchers; nothing of this kind runs afterwards.

choices.text: `watch` with `immediate: true` already set
choices.why: `immediate` is about the first run; "post" is about the redraw.

choices.text: A watcher for an HTTP POST request's answer
choices.why: Nothing to do with HTTP: post means after the redraw.

choices.text: `watchEffect` with `flush: 'post'` set
choices.why: Right: it runs after the redraw, when the page shows the change.

prompt: When the course changes, the planner must save the notes of the course just left before loading the new one's. Which tool fits, by the lesson's table?

choices.text: `watchEffect`, since it finds the course by itself
choices.why: It finds its sources, but never tells you what they were before.

choices.text: A computed of the course that saves when it recomputes
choices.why: Saving is a side effect, and a computed must only read and return.

choices.text: `watch`, because it hands over the old value
choices.why: Right. Its callback gets `(now, before)`; `watchEffect` gives no old value.

choices.text: A watcher with `flush: 'sync'`, so nothing is missed
choices.why: Timing is not the problem; the callback needs the old course, which `watch` gives with any flush.

prompt: Why is `'pre'` the default `flush`, running a watcher before the redraw?

choices.text: Because the page is not yet built when a watcher is created
choices.why: Creation is not the point; this is about every change after it.

choices.text: Because it sees every intermediate value, which `post` cannot
choices.why: That is `sync`; `pre` ran once with the final value.

choices.text: So that state it sets is drawn in one pass, not two
choices.why: Right: one pass instead of two, and most watchers do not touch the page anyway.

choices.text: Because a watcher that reads the DOM needs the old page
choices.why: Reading the DOM is the job of `post`, which sees the page after the change.

prompt: One click on `Add two` in `FlushTiming`, which increments `count` twice. Put the lines in the order they were printed.
trap: `'sync'` runs at each write, `'pre'` once before the redraw, `'post'` once after it.

prompt: A teammate puts `v-focus` on the search field of the planner's week page, so that the cursor is there the moment the page loads. What does the lesson say about it?

prompt: A parent writes `class="wide"` on a component whose template has two root elements and no `v-bind="$attrs"`. Where does the class go?

choices.text: Nowhere, with a warning

choices.text: Injects the rules into the page, then puts them in a file of their own

prompt: How do libraries such as the router make themselves available to every component of an application?

prompt: With no provider above it, `SessionRow` shows `statistics` where the title would be. Why does the lesson choose that over an empty string?

prompt: The router changes the page and `afterEach` sets `document.title`. What does a blind student hear, by the lesson?

choices.text: It runs when the application mounts, since a store belongs to the app

choices.text: Pinia turns it into an action
choices.why: Pinia makes actions of the functions a store returns; a hook call is not one.
